nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\alpha$, the language over $\alpha$ denoted by a generalized regular expression over $\alpha$ is defined recursively, for generalized regular expressions $e$, $e_1$, $e_2$: an ordinary regular expression denotes the language it matches; the complement $\neg e$ denotes the complement, in the set of all words over $\alpha$, of the language of $e$; the union $e_1 + e_2$ denotes the union and the…
nodes.title: Language of a generalized regular expression

nodes.summary: A generalized regular expression over an alphabet $\alpha$ is built from ordinary regular expressions over $\alpha$ by complement, union, concatenation and Kleene star: every ordinary regular expression over $\alpha$ is one, and if $e$, $e_1$, $e_2$ are generalized regular expressions, then so are the complement $\neg e$, the union $e_1 + e_2$, the concatenation $e_1 e_2$ and the star $e^*$.
nodes.title: Generalized regular expressions

nodes.summary: A language $L$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ has generalized star height at most $n$, for a natural number $n$, if some generalized regular expression over $\alpha$ whose generalized star height is at most $n$ denotes $L$.
nodes.title: Bounded generalized star height

nodes.summary: The star height of an ordinary regular expression is the nesting depth of the Kleene star in it: the expressions for the empty language and the empty word and the single letters have star height $0$; a union $e_1 + e_2$ and a concatenation $e_1 e_2$ have the larger of the star heights of $e_1$ and $e_2$; and $e^*$ has star height one more than $e$.
nodes.title: Star height of a regular expression

nodes.summary: The generalized star height of a generalized regular expression is the nesting depth of the Kleene star in it, counting the stars inside its ordinary regular subexpressions: for generalized regular expressions $e$, $e_1$, $e_2$, an ordinary regular expression has its usual star height; the complement $\neg e$ has the star height of $e$; the union $e_1 + e_2$ and the concatenation $e_1 e_2$ have the larger of the…

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
